name: Raw Raman measurement files (54 spectra, 532/780 nm excitation) of 49 ocean polymer specimens (Miller et al. 2022, Scientific Data 9:780)
description: The 54 distinct raw Raman measurements of the 49-specimen subset of the Miller et al. 2022 ocean-polymer library (Scientific Data 9, 780, doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01883-5; deposit https://osf.io/7cqv4/, license note as in ocean_polymers) - the unprocessed counterpart of the ocean_polymers key. The files of Data1_raw_csv.zip are Thermo/Nicolet Omnic exports (line 1 'Created As Omnic File,<CODE>', line 2 'Raman Shift / cm-1,INT', data rows in DESCENDING wavenumber order - flipped to ascending by the loader). The zip holds 87 files, but 33 are byte-identical copies of another file under an instrument-run prefix (e.g. '24544r56_1 PLAS 214 532 nm.csv' = 'PLAS 214 532 nm.csv'); the loader keeps one of each. Two excitation wavelengths are present: 41 spectra at 532 nm (3,467 points, 76.55-3,418.58 cm^-1) and 13 at 780 nm (2,700 points, 200.49-3,699.66 cm^-1); every spectrum is linearly interpolated onto the common 201-3,418 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid (3,218 points; the intersection of the two native axes). 49 specimen codes: 36 measured at 532 nm only, 8 at 780 nm only and 5 at both -> is_grouped=True with group_id = specimen code, so group-aware splits keep a specimen's two spectra together. Task: classification of anthropogenic polymers (PLAS-coded, 41 spectra) vs biological materials (BIOL-coded, 13 spectra) - the paper's central identification question. Intensities are raw counts with no normalization: absolute scales differ per excitation (532 nm: -511..29,382; 780 nm: -123..1,104), and the 8 specimens measured at 780 nm only are 5 BIOL and 3 PLAS, so excitation and class are partially confounded. The raw axis extends beyond the common window at both ends (truncation as in the ocean_polymers key's 200-3,400 cm^-1 grid). Downloaded directly from OSF's stable file URL (size + sha256 pinned); no mirror required.

rai:dataCollection: Raw Raman measurements (532 nm and 780 nm excitation) of 49 ocean polymer specimens recorded for the reference library; Omnic exports with a descending wavenumber axis and raw counts.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: No preprocessing was applied by the authors (raw Omnic counts). The raman_data loader only skips the two header rows, flips the descending wavenumber axis to ascending, and linearly interpolates onto the common 201-3,418 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid (3,218 points); no baseline correction, smoothing or normalization is applied.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are derived from the specimen codes in the deposit's filenames: PLAS-coded specimens -> anthropogenic polymer (41 spectra), BIOL-coded specimens -> biological material (13 spectra); no re-labelling was performed for this benchmark.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All samples are polymer specimens and biological marine materials (bones, chitin, tissues, etc.).
rai:dataBiases: Small and imbalanced class sizes (41 vs 13); the absolute intensity scale differs per excitation wavelength (532 nm: -511..29,382 counts; 780 nm: -123..1,104 counts), so a model can in principle exploit the excitation signature; the 8 specimens measured at 780 nm only are 5 biological and 3 anthropogenic, partially confounding excitation with class. Only 49 of the 79 library specimens have raw files deposited; the 532 nm and 780 nm spectra of the 5 specimens measured at both are correlated, hence the specimen-level grouping.
rai:dataLimitations: Raw counts without normalization; non-comparable absolute scales across excitation wavelengths; partial excitation-vs-class confound (8 of 49 specimens measured at 780 nm only); imbalanced classes (41 vs 13); the two spectra of a specimen measured at both wavelengths are correlated (grouping provided); the 3,218-point common window truncates each native axis (532 nm loses 76.55-201 cm^-1, 780 nm loses 3,418.58-3,699.66 cm^-1); the OSF project sets no explicit license (the open-access paper's CC BY 4.0 is applied).
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports marine plastic pollution research: anthropogenic-vs-biological discrimination of marine debris on raw (unprocessed) spectra, including the 780 nm excitation set; environmental monitoring use, no human or medical data.
rai:dataUseCases: Binary classification (anthropogenic polymer vs biological material) on raw Raman spectra with group-aware splitting on specimen code; robustness studies across excitation wavelengths (532 vs 780 nm); preprocessing and domain-adaptation benchmarks (raw vs the post-processed ocean_polymers key).
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Data collection: Raman spectra of ocean polymer specimens for the reference library 'A Raman spectral reference library of potential anthropogenic and biological ocean polymers' (Emily A. Miller, Kevan M. Yamahara, Chris French, Neil E. Spingarn, James M. Birch, Kyle S. Van Houtan 2022, Scientific Data 9, 780, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01883-5, open access CC BY 4.0; data deposited at https://osf.io/7cqv4/, public OSF node 7cqv4, no child components). The library covers 40 pristine anthropogenic polymers newly sourced from manufacturers, 22 weathered anthropogenic polymers from used consumer, beachcast, agricultural and fishery sources, and 17 biological polymers representing diverse marine taxa, trophic levels and tissues. License note: The OSF project page sets no explicit license; the open-access parent paper (Scientific Data, CC BY 4.0) publishes the data records in its Data Records section, which is the license applied here. This raman_data key loads the deposit's raw file Data1_raw_csv.zip (1,452,113 bytes, size + sha256 pinned, downloaded directly from OSF's stable file URL): 87 Thermo/Nicolet Omnic measurement files of 49 specimen codes - the unprocessed counterpart of the ocean_polymers key. 33 of the 87 files are byte-identical copies of another file under an instrument-run prefix, so the loader keeps 54 distinct spectra: 41 at 532 nm (3,467 points, 76.55-3,418.58 cm^-1) and 13 at 780 nm (2,700 points, 200.49-3,699.66 cm^-1); raw counts, no normalization; the wavenumber axis is stored descending in each file (flipped to ascending by the loader). Every spectrum is linearly interpolated onto the common 201-3,418 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid (3,218 points; intersection of the two native axes). 36 specimen codes were measured at 532 nm only, 8 at 780 nm only and 5 at both (is_grouped=True, group_id = specimen code).
